narrative.northStar: The Rhodonite Specimen, put to work
narrative.overview:
The tools are cut from the same stone as itrium.id. That site is The Rhodonite Specimen (`DESIGN.md` in the `website` repository): a graphite matrix with a pink vein, where gray is the body and pink marks what a visitor should find. Here the specimen leaves the display case and goes onto the workbench. The world is the same: Plus Jakarta Sans for everything, graphite and paper, pastel pink with its two deepenings, flat tonal surfaces, pills and soft corners, one drawn arrow. Only the job changes. itrium.id persuades; a tool gets out of the way.

The index is The Rantang: a stacked enamel food carrier seen from the front. Graphite enamel owns the page in both themes. The header's thick arc is the carrying handle, its two ends run down into the rails that frame the tiers, and the tiers stack on one measured module with a lighter rolled rim along each top edge. The lid carries Flint's name and one line. Each tool is a tier: its symbol, its name at display size, what it does, and, before anyone presses, what leaves it, with its pink start, the latch. The base tier says what never leaves. Privacy is the object's construction, said on the tier it concerns, not claimed in a list. A tool page keeps the header (the handle's links, without the arc) and below it is unchanged from the map that came before: a place mark for a title, the work directly under it, and the tool's one road out hanging from the control that takes it, because the person using it is at a restaurant table with a phone in one hand and a group waiting. Whether the tool pages take the Rantang too is an open decision for the owner.

Components are soft and sure-footed, and tactile without being playful. Every control has a round, generous target that a thumb finds the first time (2.75rem on touch screens) and an edge you can see (3:1 against the page and the card). They feel good to press but never perform. Density on the index is bold and wide, a carrier you hold; inside a tool it is calm and working: forms sit in a narrow column of 36 to 42rem, inset lists and notes nest one tonal step down inside cards, and the running total stays at the bottom of a phone's screen while the bill is made.

Light and dark are equal. Each follows the visitor's system unless the footer says otherwise, and neither is a courtesy version of the other: every new pairing is designed and checked in both. The system refuses what itrium.id refuses: generic SaaS ornament (gradient text, icon-card rows, invented numbers), drop shadows on anything but a floating list, pure black and white, decorative pink, and small labels above headings. It refuses what only a tool can get wrong: a hero that pushes the tool off a phone screen, and state shown by color alone. And on the index it refuses anything that reads as a receipt: the owner turned down the line-item strip (#70) and the Device Map (#71) for dashed lines, gray-on-paper monochrome, a narrow stacked column, and the feel as a whole.
keyCharacteristics: One stone with itrium.id: the same tokens, typeface, radii, button shapes and arrow.

The index is one carrier: a handle arc (the page's only arc), two rails, and graphite tiers on an 18.5rem module, 8px apart, each with a rolled rim. Graphite in both themes, with dark mode's text colors inside it.
Each tool has one fixed symbol, drawn in the text color, the same in the header and on its tier.
Pink only at the two latches on the index (equal starts), and at one primary action per tool view.
A tool page opens with a place mark, then the tool, with its one road out drawn under the control that takes it.
Light and dark are equal. Both follow the system, unless System, Light or Dark is chosen in the footer.
Flat surfaces with tonal steps. The only shadow is under the open searchable list.
Every control has a 3:1 edge (`--control-border`), a target at least 2.75rem tall on touch screens, and 16px text on touch screens so iOS doesn't zoom.
Motion is CSS only and off under reduced motion.

rules.name: The Vein Rule
rules.body: Pink marks something: the primary action, focus, what's selected, or the way onward. If you can't say what a pink element marks, it should be gray. Pink means one thing at a time, which is not the same as one element. In a tool, one pink button per view. On the index, one pink latch on each tool's tier, the two tools' equal starts ("Split a bill", "Chat with a number"): one meaning, two pills. Rose-text action lines serve the tools elsewhere and a shared bill as their way onward, and nothing else is pink. The handle, rails, rims, tool symbols, a tool page's place mark and its road out are never pink.

rules.name: The Enamel Rule
rules.body: Inside a tier (the `.enamel` scope), dark mode's colors apply in both themes: off-white text, muted gray on dark, pink focus and pink edges, and the dark control edge. The enamel is graphite either way, so its contents never take light mode's graphite text, rose text or deep-rose edges.

rules.name: The Two Borders Rule
rules.body: `--border` is for lines nothing depends on, such as card edges and dividers. Anything a person has to find in order to use it gets `--control-border`.

rules.name: The Graphite Text Rule
rules.body: Text on pink is graphite, never white. On light backgrounds pink text is rose text and pink lines are deep rose. Pastel pink is never text or a line there.

rules.name: The Every-Surface Rule
rules.body: Contrast is checked on every surface text sits on: page, card, inset list, note, running total, update notice, each tier and the page around the carrier, in both themes. Text needs 4.5:1. Focus outlines, control edges and state lines need 3:1. Dark mode's tier (`graphite-raised`) is the tightest: text 12.5:1, muted 4.6:1, pink 8.0:1, control edge 3.1:1.

rules.name: The One Typeface Rule
rules.body: Plus Jakarta Sans does everything. Never add a second family, and never load a font from another domain.

rules.name: The No Kicker Rule
rules.body: A heading is the first thing in its block. No eyebrow, category label, small uppercase heading or back link sits above it. Nothing here is set in uppercase. A line that says more about a heading goes under it or beside it, as the lid's line does. A tier's symbol sits above its name, but it is the tool's picture, not a label.

rules.name: The One Carrier Rule
rules.body: The index is one carrier: a handle, two rails, and tiers on one module. A new tool is a new tier, the same height as the others, with its symbol, its name, what it does, what leaves it and its own pink latch. No cards, no rows of entries, no hero over equal tiers.

rules.name: The Kept Space Rule
rules.body: What the browser remembers arrives into a space already kept for it (what a tool does keeps two lines, 3.5rem; the shared bill's line keeps 3rem on phones and 2.5rem from 768 px), so nothing moves under a finger when it appears.

rules.name: The Slab Rule, for tools
rules.body: A tool page has no slab at either end: it opens with a place mark, a dot and the tool's name, and never closes with a panel. On a phone, the tool comes before the frame.

rules.name: The First Screen Rule
rules.body: On a phone, the first field of a tool is visible without scrolling, and on the index the first tier's latch is. If a new element would push either down, it belongs lower on the page.

rules.name: The Answer In Reach Rule
rules.body: Wherever a tool is being filled in, its answer is one glance or one tap away: the running total below 1024 px, the split's own column above. Someone opening a shared result lands on it, not on the form that made it.

rules.name: The Only Floating Things Cast Shadows Rule
rules.body: Tiers, rims, the handle, cards, buttons, chips, bands, the road boxes and the running total never get a drop shadow. A control responds by filling with the next tonal step, a tier by lifting its rim, a header link by its underline, and an arrow by moving 4 px on.

rules.name: The One Arc Rule
rules.body: The handle is the index's only arc. Corners are rounded and the rails have rounded feet, but no other element on the page sweeps a curve.

rules.name: The Pinned Fact Rule
rules.body: What leaves a tool is said on that tool's tier, beside its latch, before anyone presses it. What never leaves is said once, on the base. Never collect them into a legend or a list apart from the tools they concern.

rules.name: The Hanging Road Rule
rules.body: A road out hangs from the one control that takes it, and only where the site really makes the connection. A friend's "Copy the link" copies the link they opened, which goes nowhere new, so no road is drawn under it.

rules.name: The Whole Edge Rule
rules.body: A note is marked by its whole edge, never by a thick bar down one side.

dos: Do take tokens, radii, button shapes, the arrow and type roles from itrium.id's DESIGN.md before inventing anything. A difference between the two sites needs a reason a tool has and a page doesn't.
Do add to the index as the Rantang: a new tool is a new tier on the same 18.5rem module, 8px from the next, with its symbol, its name, what it does, what leaves it, and its own pink latch.
Do keep the enamel graphite in both themes, with dark mode's text, muted, focus and control edge colors inside it (`.enamel`).
Do give every tool one symbol and use it wherever the tool is named in the frame: the header and its tier.
Do keep the rim's lift to 4px, motion-safe only, on a tier whose latch is hovered or focused.
Do keep a tool's first field, and the index's first latch, on the first phone screen.
Do give every field, button and chip a `--control-border` edge and a touch target at least 2.75rem tall on touch screens.

Do show every state in two ways: a check mark with the pink fill, words with the pink edge, an underline on the current page's link, and the reason a button can't be pressed yet, said under it when someone presses or reaches it (not at rest, and not read out again after every add).
Do design and check every new pairing in light and dark, on every surface it sits on.
Do use the drawn arrow wherever a link points onward.

Do keep motion in CSS, gated on `motion-safe` or `prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference`: page cross-fades, the rim's lift, the 4 px arrow nudge, and the loading spinner. Nothing rises or reveals as it scrolls.
Do open a tool page with its place mark, and hang the tool's road out from the control that takes it, saying the same fact as its tier on the index.
Do use Tailwind classes with the theme tokens and the shared classes in `src/lib/styles.ts`, never raw hex values in markup.
donts: Don't make the index read as a receipt, on any cue: no dashed lines, no gray-on-paper monochrome, no narrow stacked column, no rows of entries, ledgers, departure boards or maps. The owner turned down the line-item strip (#70) and the Device Map (#71) for exactly this.
Don't put cards, a legend, a hero over equal tiers, or a second arc on the index.

Don't use pink as decoration, or give pink two meanings in one view: a tool has one pink button, and the index's two latches are both the primary action, one on each tool's tier. The handle, rails, rims and symbols are never pink.

Don't add a structural gray outside the palette. Its two exceptions, the band's raised border (#4f4f4f) and the enamel's rim and frame in dark mode (#575757), are each a structural step above a palette gray; a new one needs the same reason, and a color change otherwise belongs in `@itrium/palettes`.
Don't put a small uppercase heading, eyebrow, kicker or back link above a heading.
Don't type arrows or chevrons as characters.
Don't give tiers, cards, buttons, chips, bands or the running total a drop shadow.
Don't use `#000000` or pure white text on pink. Graphite is `#2b2b2b`.
Don't put pastel pink text or lines on a light background, or rose text and deep-rose lines inside a tier.
Don't use a native `<select>`, inline styles, `data:` URLs, or anything from another domain.
Don't add gradient text, icon-card rows, invented numbers, or a hero that pushes the tool off a phone screen.
Don't set field text below 16px on touch screens.
Don't put a band behind a tool's title: the band is the error page's alone.
